s2.p1: **JS** cannot be strictly called an object-oriented language because it violates some principles of object-oriented programming. The prototype-based inheritance model essentially involves delegation rather than inheritance as understood in languages with a class-based inheritance model.
s2.p2: ☼☼☼ In JS, functions rule, not classes ☼☼☼.
s3.p1: If you want to experience true **polymorphism**, you need JS.
s3.p2: Here, polymorphism starts from the very first step.
s3.p3: In JavaScript, polymorphism manifests itself through various mechanisms such as function overloading, prototypical inheritance, and dynamic typing. These features make JS a powerful and flexible development tool.

s4.p1:
**JS** incorporates many nice features from **functional programming languages** (such as _chaining computations_, _currying_).

Func-style in JS is a direct consequence of the aforementioned, and importantly, it forms the foundation of asynchrony.
s4.p3: In short, JS is built on functions, and this is not just a principle of executing individual tasks, but rather a way of the language's existence, its main essence. The main features of the language - prototype-based inheritance and asynchrony - are implemented through functions.
s5.slogan1: JS - it's jazz, it's improvisation, it's fantastic freedom.
s5.p2: It's essential to deeply understand what the engine will do when interpreting your line of code.
s5.p3: The engine is powerful, so putting someone who can't drive behind the wheel of an HMMWV is complete madness.
s5.p4:
Even worse is letting a novice "steer" an F35.

Dive in, guys! With persistence and patience.
s5.slogan2: Have a great flight with JS!
